From: Wen Li (Property Manager)
To: Owners' Committee, Larch House
Subject: Leak into unit 2C

On 12 October the tenant in 2C reported water coming through the bathroom ceiling. The plumber (invoice $640) found a cracked supply pipe inside the wall of unit 3C's bathroom. The pipe serves only 3C and the crack is on the 3C side of 3C's shut-off valve. Repairing the 2C ceiling is quoted at $1,150.

Bylaws:
(a) Pipes serving only one unit, on the unit side of that unit's shut-off valve, are the unit owner's responsibility.
(b) Common pipes and risers are the association's responsibility.
(c) Whoever is responsible for the source pays for the resulting damage to other units, unless the damage is claimed on the building insurance, which has a $2,500 deductible per claim, payable by the responsible party.

The owner of 3C, Mr. Haas, says the pipe failed through age, that he did nothing wrong, and that the association should pay. The committee meets on 20 October.

Wen

q1.instructions: Under the bylaws, who is responsible for the cracked pipe?

criteria.3C owner: Mr. Haas, as owner of unit 3C

q2.instructions: Who should pay for the 2C ceiling repair?

criteria.Insurance claim: Claim it on the building insurance
criteria.Split cost: The association and Mr. Haas share it

q3.instructions: How do the total costs of this leak compare with the insurance deductible?

criteria.Below deductible: The total is less than the deductible, so a claim would pay nothing
criteria.Above deductible: The total is more than the deductible, so a claim would pay out

q4.instructions: How should the committee answer Mr. Haas?

criteria.Association pays: Agree that the association will pay
criteria.Cite bylaw (a): Explain that bylaw (a) makes him responsible whatever the cause
criteria.Goodwill half: Offer to pay half as a goodwill gesture
criteria.Legal advice: Refer the question to a lawyer before replying
criteria.Defer: Put off a decision until next year's meeting
criteria.Ask insurer: Ask the insurer to decide who pays

[08:32] Mei: Our end-of-line leak test runs at 1.5 bar and passed every part. Aldane tests at 3 bar. We have a 3 bar test rig that can do about 150 parts per shift.
[08:40] Rita (Logistics): 600 pieces of lot 2611 are still in our warehouse; the other 600 are at Aldane. Lots 2612 and 2613 (cast 5-8 June, degasser running) are also here, 2,000 pieces.

criteria.Test pressure: Our leak test runs at a lower pressure than Aldane's

criteria.Rework all: Send all 600 for impregnation rework without testing
criteria.Ship with note: Ship them with a warning note to Aldane
criteria.Test a sample: Test 20 pieces at 3 bar and release the lot if they pass

criteria.Quarantine, replace: Set them aside and use replacement housings from lots 2612-2613 shipped now

criteria.Stop their line: Stop Aldane's line until the investigation ends
criteria.Use and monitor: Use them and watch for more leaks
